newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER FINAL IN ITALY SEES NORTH-SOUTH VIOLENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER FINAL IN ITALY SEES NORTH-SOUTH VIOLENCE.

text.p: Around 30 people were hurt in clashes on Thursday night when the Italian soccer cup final between Vicenza and Napoli turned into a north-south battle.
Police on Friday said the injured included a 25-year-old Vicenza fan who was stabbed in the leg outside the stadium after the northern club beat Napoli 3-0.

Helmeted riot police baton-charged the Napoli end of the Romeo Menti stadium when fighting broke out after the final whistle. Most of the injured, none of them serious, were Napoli fans, hospital sources said.
Around 3,000 supporters had travelled north from the southern port of Naples for the game, which carried strong racist overtones.
Banners and slogans supporting the Northern League party, which is campaigning for a separate state in affluent northern Italy, were in evidence at the match.
One compared Naples unfavourably with the Albanian capital Tirana and another said "No to immigration".
Napoli supporters had hurled red flares and fireworks directly at Vicenza fans throughout the match.
Vicenza is in the northeast Veneto region, where the frustration with central government and high taxes that has fuelled separatist sentiment runs high.
The League, and smaller separatist groups, have sought to depict southerners as lazy and criminal and complain that taxes on earnings in the north subsidise the less developed south.
Vicenza won Thursday's game after extra time to take their first trophy in their 95-year history. They won the final 3-1 on aggregate after Napoli had beaten them 1-0 in the first leg.
